# odyssey-038 (8.487–586) — adversarial review

Two passes over `units.json` and `gloss.json` (51 units, 154 gloss keys incl. `__broaden__`); `t` never touched (checked: every `t` identical to the backup, and the units still rebuild the archive lines 487–586 exactly). No line was flagged for scansion in the packet, so nothing was scanned by hand and no metre sentence was added. No modern translation consulted.

Checks that passed with no change: line division of `l` = `t` in all 51 units, no `\n` in any `i`; `p` on the four Murray paragraphs (487, 499, 521, 536); `mark` on 487 (Odysseus speaks) and 536 (Alcinous speaks); “ on the first unit of each speech (487, 536) and ” on the last (498, 586); 037's last unit (ends 8.486 with the introduction, no opening mark) hands over correctly to the opening of 487; Alcinous' speech ends at 586, the end of Book 8, so nothing spans into part 039; the reported words of Nausithous (564–569) are indirect and carry no inner marks. Repeated lines: 532–534 and 535 identical to the published `l` and `i`; 572 identical; 536 first line identical; 513 third line of `l` identical to the published wording. Every word of the 100 lines has a gloss key (this file or known-forms); no orphan keys. Cross-references checked: 508/504 ἐρύσαντας, 511/569 ἀμφικαλύψ-, 503/562 κεκαλυμμέν-, 515/526 ἐκχύμενοι/χυμένη, 523/531 simile, 530/531 ἐλεεινός, 489/578 οἶτος, 537/542 σχεθέτω, 543/549 κάλλιον, 544/546 τέτυκται, 584/586 πεπνυμένα εἰδῇ, 1.2, 1.169, 4.273, 7.186, 8.93–96 — all true.

## Considered and refused

- 504 l "had dragged" for the aorist ἐρύσαντο: pluperfect in both layers reflects the explanatory γάρ; consistent, no sense lost.
- 539–541 i "has not once ceased" for οὔ πω παύσατο: the force (not yet stopped since we began) is carried; refused as a paraphrase, not an error.
- 4 and 43 notes "θεός has no article, so 'a god'": true of the form; Homeric articlelessness is the reason given, and the note already flags the ambiguity at 498.
- 492 note "δῖος … always so rendered": house policy, not a claim about the poem.
- 516 note "Deiphobus … a son of Priam" and gloss Ναυσίθοος "father of Alcinous": cultural facts, the second stated in the line itself (564–565).
- 577 l "within in your heart": a literal gloss of ἔνδοθι θυμῷ, awkward but faithful; `i` is natural.
- 573 l "well-inhabited" against i "well-peopled": same sense, no table row fixes it.
- 519 i "the most dread of wars": stays; built from αἰνότατον + πόλεμον, no remembered phrase found.
- 500 i "taking up the tale": built from ἑλών + the ὡς-clause; not a remembered phrase.
- 550 note "κατὰ ἄστυ 'through the town'" against l "in the town": both fine for κατά + acc.; left.
- 546 i "For a man who …": "for" is the preposition (dative of interest), not a connective added to an asyndeton; left.
- ἀντίθεος, περικλυτός, μεγάθυμος, ἀοιδός, φόρμιγξ λίγεια, πεπνυμένα εἰδῇ, Δαναοί/Ἀργεῖοι, ἄγριος, κακὰ etc.: checked against the table; all agree.
- new-renderings.md: every row checked against the conventions table and the units (line numbers, `l`, `i`, avoided words); no conflicts with existing rows (the δόρυ "timber" avoidance belongs to the palm-trunk row at 6.167 and does not apply to the horse at 8.507).
- Nested/indirect speech (Nausithous, 564–569): no marks added, per convention that only direct speech is quoted.
